newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta firmer in late trade after rocky session.
newsitem.headline: Peseta firmer in late trade after rocky session.

text.p: The peseta firmed slightly in late trade on Monday after a rocky session which saw the Bank of Spain intervening to hold the currency off the 85.00 per mark level.
By 1645 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.79/82 per mark, compared with levels seen late on Friday of 84.92/95.

Comments from Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer and EMI head Alexander Lamfalussy that EMU's start date would not be delayed helped calm the market at midday and lent some support to the peseta, traders said.

Earlier in the session, the peseta came under pressure forcing the Bank of Spain to intervene. The central bank bought pesetas for marks at around 84.95 to prevent the Spanish currency from weakening through 85.00 per mark.
"The market was quite calm after the comments on monetary union which supported peripheral currencies," said one dealer.
Against the dollar, the peseta was trading at 143.87/92 compared with early levels of 143.85/97.
